children.translated_text: Having bowed with speech, body, and mind to <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, the teacher of the world,
<s>Aśvaghoṣa</s> composes the <s>Vajrasūcī</s> according to [his] understanding. || 1 ||

children.text: vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ smṛtayaḥ pramāṇaṃ dharmārthayuktaṃ vacanaṃ pramāṇam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> are authoritative; the <s>Smṛtis</s> (traditional law codes) are authoritative; speech that is consistent with <s>dharma</s> and purpose is authoritative.

children.text: yasya pramāṇaṃ na bhavetpramāṇaṃ kastasya kuryādvacanaṃ pramāṇam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: He for whom authority itself would not be authoritative — who would make his word authoritative? || 2 ||
Seven hunters [were reborn] in <s>Daśārṇa</s>; deer on Mount <s>Kālañjara</s>;
<s>cakravāka</s> birds on the island of <s>Śarat</s>; swans on Lake <s>Mānasa</s>. || 3 ||

body.translated_text: Even they were born [again] in <s>Kurukṣetra</s> as <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who had mastered the <s>Vedas</s>. || 4 ||

children.translated_text: Having studied the four <s>Vedas</s> with their limbs (<s>aṅga</s>) and subsidiary parts (<s>upāṅga</s>),
a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who accepts gifts from a <s>Śūdra</s> is reborn as a donkey. || 5 ||
A donkey for twelve births, a pig for sixty births,
a dog for seventy births — thus spoke <s>Manu</s>. || 6 ||
<s>Acala</s> was born from a she-elephant; <s>Keśapiṅgala</s> from an owl;
<s>Agastya</s> from the <s>Agasti</s> flower; <s>Kauśika</s> was born from <s>kuśa</s> grass. || 7 ||
<s>Kapila</s> was born from a she-monkey (<s>kapilā</s>); <s>Gautama</s> from a clump of reeds (<s>śaragulma</s>);
<s>Droṇācārya</s> from a water-vessel (<s>kalaśa</s>); <s>Tittiri</s> was the offspring of a partridge (<s>tittirī</s>). || 8 ||
<s>Reṇukā</s> gave birth to <s>Rāma</s> [<s>Paraśurāma</s>]; a doe gave birth to the sage <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>;
a fisherwoman gave birth to <s>Vyāsa</s>; and a <s>Śūdra</s> woman [gave birth to] <s>Kuśika</s>. || 9 ||

children.text: viśvāmitraṃ ca caṇḍālī vasiṣṭhaṃ caiva urvaśī /
children.translated_text: And a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> woman [gave birth to] <s>Viśvāmitra</s>; and <s>Urvaśī</s> [gave birth to] <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: na teṣāṃ brāhmaṇī mātā lokācārācca brāhmaṇāḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: Their mothers were not <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> women, yet by worldly convention they are [called] <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 10 ||

children.text: sadyaḥ patati māṃsena lākṣayā lavaṇena ca /
children.translated_text: A [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] falls immediately [from his status] by [selling] meat, lac, or salt;
and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who sells milk becomes a <s>Śūdra</s> after three days. || 11 ||
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who travel through the sky fall from eating meat.

children.text: viprāṇāṃ patanaṃ dṛṣṭvā tato māṃsāni varjayet || 12 ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the fall of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, therefore one should abstain from meat. || 12 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇatvaṃ na śāstreṇa na saṃskārairna jātibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood is not [determined] by scripture, nor by <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory rites), nor by birth (<s>jāti</s>),

children.text: na kulena na vedena na karmaṇā bhavettataḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: nor by family (<s>kula</s>), nor by <s>Vedas</s>, nor by [ritual] actions — therefore [what determines it?] || 13 ||
Free from possessiveness (<s>nirmama</s>), free from ego (<s>nirahaṃkāra</s>), unattached (<s>niḥsaṅga</s>), without acquisitions (<s>niṣparigraha</s>),
liberated from passion and hatred — him the gods know as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 14 ||

children.text: satyaṃ brahma tapo brahma brahma cendriyanigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Truth is <s>Brahman</s>; austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is <s>Brahman</s>; and sense-control (<s>indriyanigraha</s>) is <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: sarvabhūte dayā brahma etad brāhmaṇa lakṣaṇam || 15 ||
children.translated_text: compassion toward all beings is <s>Brahman</s> — this is the mark of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 15 ||

children.text: satyaṃ nāsti tapo nāsti nāsti cendriyanigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is no truth, no austerity, no sense-control,
no compassion toward all beings — that is the mark of a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste). || 16 ||
Among women of gods, humans, and [beings in] animal wombs,

children.text: maithunaṃ nādhigacchanti te viprāste ca brāhmaṇāḥ || 17 ||
children.translated_text: those who do not engage in sexual intercourse — they are the learned ones, they are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 17 ||
Birth (<s>jāti</s>) is not seen [to matter]; it is virtuous qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) that bring about good.

children.text: caṇḍālo 'pi hi tatrasthastaṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: Even a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> established in those [virtues] — him the gods know as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 18 ||
For one who has drunk the foam [from the lips] of a <s>Vṛṣalī</s> (low-caste woman), who is defiled by her breath,
and who is born in that [low-caste environment] — no expiation is found. || 19 ||
One who eats continuously for one month from the hand of a <s>Śūdra</s> woman —
while alive he becomes a <s>Śūdra</s>; when dead, he is reborn as a dog. || 20 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is surrounded by <s>Śūdra</s> [women] and whose household [is managed by] a <s>Śūdra</s> wife,
abandoned by the ancestors (<s>Pitṛ</s>) and gods — he goes to <s>Raurava</s> [hell]. || 21 ||
Born from the womb of a fire-churning stick (<s>araṇī</s>), the great sage named <s>Kaṭha</s>
became a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through austerity — therefore birth is not the cause. || 22 ||
Born from the womb of a fisherwoman, the great sage named <s>Vyāsa</s>
became a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through austerity — therefore birth is not the cause. || 23 ||
Born from the womb of <s>Urvaśī</s>, the great sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> too
became a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through austerity — therefore birth is not the cause. || 24 ||
Born from the womb of a doe, the great sage <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>
became a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through austerity — therefore birth is not the cause. || 25 ||
Born from the womb of a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> woman, the great sage <s>Viśvāmitra</s>
became a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through austerity — therefore birth is not the cause. || 26 ||
Born from the womb of a maidservant (<s>tāṇḍūlī</s>), the great sage <s>Nārada</s>
became a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through austerity — therefore birth is not the cause. || 27 ||

body.text:
jitātmā yatirbhavati..................... jitendriyaḥ /
[yatātmā yatirbhavati vijitātmā(jitātmā ca)jitendriyaḥ /]

children.translated_text: through austerity one becomes an ascetic (<s>tāpasa</s>); through celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) one becomes a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 28 ||

body.translated_text: One who has conquered the self becomes an ascetic (<s>yati</s>)...... one who has conquered the senses;

children.text: na ca te brāhmaṇīputrāste ca lokasya brāhmaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: And they are not sons of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> women, yet they are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> to the world.
Virtuous conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and purity (<s>śauca</s>) constitute <s>Brahman</s> — therefore family (<s>kula</s>) is not the cause. || 29 ||

children.text: śīlaṃ pradhānaṃ na kulaṃ pradhānaṃ kulena kiṃ śīlavivarjitena /
children.translated_text: Moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) is foremost, not family lineage. What use is lineage devoid of moral conduct?

children.text: bahavo narā nīcakula prasūtāḥ svargaṃ gatāḥ śīlamupetya dhīrāḥ || 30 ||
children.translated_text: Many men born of low families, having attained moral conduct, have gone to heaven — the steadfast ones. || 30 ||
From the mouth [of <s>Brahman</s>], a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was born; from the arms, a <s>kṣatriya</s> likewise;

children.text: urubhyāṃ vaiśyaḥ saṃjātaḥ padbhyāṃ śūdraka eva ca || 31 ||
children.translated_text: from the thighs, a <s>vaiśya</s> was born; from the feet, a <s>śūdra</s> indeed. || 31 ||

children.text: pāṇḍostu viśrutaḥ putraḥ sa vai nāmnā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ /
children.translated_text: The renowned son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> — he who is known by the name <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> —
having approached <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, asks with joined palms: || 32 ||

children.text: ke ca te brāhmaṇāḥ proktāḥ kiṃ vā brāhmaṇalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: "Who are those called <s>brāhmaṇas</s>? And what is the mark of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>?

children.text: etadicchāmi bho jñātuṃ tad bhavān vyākaroti me || 33 ||
children.translated_text: This I wish to know, sir — please explain it to me." || 33 ||
"Endowed with qualities such as patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) and the rest, one who has abandoned the rod [of punishment], free from [desire for] meat,
who does not harm any living being — this is the first mark of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 34 ||

children.text: yadā sarvaṃ paradravyaṃ pathi vā yadi vā gṛhe /
children.translated_text: When one does not take what is not given — another's property, whether on the road or in the house —
this is the second mark of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 35 ||
Having abandoned a cruel nature, free from possessiveness, without attachment,
one who always wanders liberated — this is the third mark of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 36 ||
With women of gods and humans, and even with those born in animal wombs,

children.text: maithunaṃ hi sadā tyaktaṃ caturthaṃ brahmalakṣaṇam || 37 ||
children.translated_text: sexual intercourse is always abandoned — this is the fourth mark of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 37 ||
Truth is purity; compassion is purity; control of the senses is purity;

children.text: sarvabhūta dayā śaucaṃ tapaḥ śaucañca pañcamam || 38 ||
children.translated_text: compassion for all beings is purity; and austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the fifth [form of] purity. || 38 ||
One who is endowed with these five marks — whoever such a twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) may be —

children.text: tamahaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ brūyāṃ śeṣāḥ śūdrā yudhiṣṭhira || 39 ||
children.translated_text: him I would call a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; the rest are <s>śūdras</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. || 39 ||

children.text: na kulena na jātyā vā kriyābhirbrāhmaṇo bhavet /
children.translated_text: Not by family, not by birth, not by rituals does one become a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: caṇḍālo 'pi hi vṛtastho brāhmaṇaḥ sa yudhiṣṭhira || 40 ||
children.translated_text: even a <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste), if established in [right] conduct, is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. || 40 ||
Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), and acceptance [of gifts] from pure [sources],

children.text: phalena na samarthaṃ ca brāhmaṇaḥ syādyudhiṣṭhira // Vs_40a //
children.translated_text: and [living on] fruit alone — such a one is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. || 40a ||
This entire world was formerly of one <s>varṇa</s> (class), O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>;
the four-fold class system (<s>cāturvarṇya</s>) was established through distinctions in actions and occupations. || 41 ||

children.text: sarve vai yonijā martyāḥ sarve mūtrapurīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: All mortals are born from a womb; all produce urine and feces;
all have the same senses and objects of the senses — therefore, it is by moral qualities that one is twice-born (<s>dvija</s>). || 42 ||
Even a <s>śūdra</s> endowed with [good] conduct and virtues becomes a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> devoid of [proper] conduct becomes lower than a <s>śūdra</s>. || 43 ||
If even a <s>śūdra</s> has crossed the terrible ocean of the five senses,
immeasurable gifts should be given to him, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. || 44 ||
Birth is not seen [as determinative], O king; it is virtues that bring about well-being.

children.text: jīvitaṃ yasya dharmārthe parārthe yasya jīvitam /
children.translated_text: One whose life is for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, whose life is for the sake of others,

children.text: ahorātraṃ caretkṣāntiṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: who practices patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) day and night — the gods know him as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 45 ||
Those who have renounced household life and are established as seekers of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>),
unattached to sensual pleasures, O son of <s>Kuntī</s> — they are <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. || 46 ||
Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), freedom from possessiveness, avoidance of killing,
cessation of passion and hatred — this is the mark of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 47 ||

children.text: kṣamā dayā damo dānaṃ satyaṃ śaucaṃ smṛtirghṛṇā /
children.translated_text: Forbearance, compassion, self-control, generosity, truth, purity, mindfulness, modesty,
learning, wisdom, and faith — this is the mark of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 48 ||
Better is a well-disciplined <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose essence is the <s>Gāyatrī</s> alone
than an undisciplined one who [knows] all four <s>Vedas</s> but eats everything and sells everything. || 49 ||
The destination attained by a celibate (<s>brahmacārin</s>) who has fasted even for a single night —
that cannot be attained by thousands of sacrifices, O <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>. || 50 ||
One who has mastered all the <s>Vedas</s> and bathed at all the sacred fords (<s>tīrthas</s>),

children.text: muktaścarati yo dharmaṃ tameva brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: who wanders freely practicing <s>dharma</s> — him alone they know as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. || 51 ||

children.text: yadā na kurute pāpaṃ sarvabhūteṣu dāruṇam /
children.translated_text: When one does no cruel evil to any living being

children.text: kāyena manasā vācā brahma sampadyate tadā || 52 ||
children.translated_text: by body, mind, or speech — then one attains <s>Brahman</s>. || 52 ||

children.text: asmābhiruktaṃ yadidaṃ dvijānāṃ mohaṃ nihantuṃ hatabuddhiṃkānām /
children.translated_text: What we have said here — to destroy the delusion of the twice-born (<s>dvijas</s>) whose understanding is impaired —

children.text: gṛhmantu santo yadi yuktametanmuñcantvathāyuktamidaṃ yadi syāt || 53 ||
children.translated_text: let the virtuous accept it if it is proper; or let them reject it if it should be improper. || 53 ||

body.translated_text: This is the work of the <s>Siddhācārya</s> (Accomplished Master) <s>Aśvaghoṣa</s>. Thus the <s>Vajrasūcī</s> (Diamond Needle) is complete. May there be auspiciousness.
